notes: These questions score the model tool choice. They are not part of the shared chat_request pin. Beer has 11 questions and travel has 11, covering find, search fts, search hybrid, pipeline, narrow_to, and walk_path. travel-walk-country-hotels is out until Country documents exist (CR-38). travel-uk-beach-pipeline is the vague-chain qualification: a stored country plus a soft beach facet, one pipeline, narrow_to on the hybrid step. A find spelling is quoted only when this lab already returned it, or when the question itself states the value. Hotel price is display-only, so no question asks for a price filter. Travel uses ZEUS_USER_TRAVEL. Beer uses ZEUS_USER_BEER.

questions.text: List beers whose style is exactly American-Style India Pale Ale.
questions.notes: Stored style spelling returned rows on beer-sample nodes, Zeus 0.9.19, 2026-10-21. The mini-schema has no ex: sample, so the question states the spelling.

questions.text: Full-text search beer descriptions for the single word lager.
questions.notes: FTS on 0.9.19 returned 3 hits. Those hits carried doc_key and an empty node id, so a non-empty item list counts as evidence.

questions.text: Find hoppy citrus beers.
questions.notes: Hybrid search returned 40 beers on 0.9.19, including Dry Hop Orange and Hop Ottin IPA.

questions.text: Beers whose style is exactly American-Style India Pale Ale: walk each one to its brewery and return the brewery names.
questions.notes: Walk path in the brief is Beer to Brewery via brewery_id. A pipeline that contains both steps satisfies this. A single-beer walk of that path is probed on beer-walk-21a-ipa. This multi-beer style walk is not that fixture, so evidence is not required.

questions.text: Show ten hoppy citrus beers as cards with name and abv. Do it in one pipeline.
questions.notes: The same plan without abort_if_empty returned 10 cards on 0.9.19 in 1.7s. abort_if_empty on the hybrid step aborted even though 40 ids came back. The harness records an aborted pipeline and does not call that a prompt miss by itself.

questions.text: Where (city and state) is 21A IPA brewed?
questions.notes: Supported on 0.9.19. Once the beer key is known, one walk: from Beer doc_key 21st_amendment_brewery_cafe-21a_ipa, path [brewery_id], return name, city, state. HTTP 200, one row: 21st Amendment Brewery Cafe, San Francisco, California. The utterance has no doc_key, so a seed search may come first. Hybrid 21A IPA's top hit was that key. The scorer does not require the path array. The answer anchor is that city and state. It is not the API score.

questions.text: List every beer made by Stone Brewing.
questions.notes: Supported when the brewery key is stone_brewing_co (name Stone Brewing Co.). stone_brewing is not the live key. Inverse path [{"inverse":"Beer.brewery_id"}], return name, abv, style, limit 8, HTTP 200. Rows included Stone IPA, abv 6.9, style American-Style India Pale Ale. A seed search may precede the walk. The scorer does not require the path array. The answer anchor is the name Stone IPA, not the full beer list.

questions.text: What beers come from Belgian breweries?
questions.notes: The forward body from Beer with where {} , path [brewery_id, country], where country=belgium is HTTP 400 on 0.9.19: an empty where is not a selector. The engine doc marks that forward terminal projection as not yet. The selective side worked: from Brewery where country=belgium, inverse Beer.brewery_id, limit 5, HTTP 200, truncated. Rows included Oude Geuze, Drie Fonteinen Kriek, and Leffe Blonde. Country where name=Belgium inverse to Brewery returned 0 rows. Evidence is not required because the textbook forward body does not return rows.

questions.text: List the beers each Colorado brewery makes.
questions.notes: The words ask for the beers, which is the walk from Colorado breweries. A count per brewery is not what group_by can return. The state value that matched is lowercase colorado. group_by as an array is HTTP 400 (expected a string). group_by brewery.name is HTTP 400 because v1 group_by is terminal-local. group_by name on the beer side returned beer-name counts (Pale Ale 3), not a count per brewery. The row form, inverse Beer.brewery_id with return name, abv, style, returns beers and does not attach the brewery name. Evidence is not required.

questions.text: Count beers by country.
questions.notes: Engine label is partial: terminal-local group_by only. The demo body from Beer where {} with group_by as an array did not execute on 0.9.19 (empty where is not a selector, and group_by must be a string). This is not a successful country rollup. Evidence is not required.

questions.text: If I wanted to plan a trip in Colorado and I wanted to visit breweries, which beers and breweries would you suggest I go to? Can you create a general itinerary for me?
questions.notes: Open plan, not one pure hop. find Brewery where state=colorado returned 40 names and was truncated. An inverse walk to Beer returns the beers. path [city] on New Belgium was closure_validated and returned 0 rows. City strings are on get metadata (Fort Collins, Boulder, Denver, and others on that page). The per-brewery count aggregate is not the fixture. Evidence is not required because an aggregate-shaped walk returns HTTP 400.

questions.text: Find hotels of type hotel whose free_parking field is true.
questions.notes: Login is ZEUS_USER_TRAVEL. On 2026-10-21, find entity_type Hotel returned 0. find entity_type hotel where free_parking true returned rows (Redbrook, Swansea, Ballycastle). free_parking 1 returned 0. The mini-schema spells the type Hotel and the field as number.

questions.text: Full-text search hotel descriptions for the single word beach.
questions.notes: The harness posts this question to collection hotel. That FTS returned 3 doc_key hits on 2026-10-21. The same call on collection nodes returned HTTP 500. A doc_key hit counts as a row.

questions.text: Find beach destination hotels. The graph type is hotel.
questions.notes: hybrid on type hotel and query beach returned Moss Beach, Santa Monica, and Carmel-by-the-Sea. type Hotel returned 0. Do not require a country equality. Hotel.price is display-only.

questions.text: Find beach destination hotels of type hotel, then walk those hotels to their country.
questions.notes: Brief path is Hotel to Country via country. On type hotel that path is HTTP 400: country is not a declared FK. from.entity_type is required. Evidence is not required.

questions.text: Show ten beach destination hotels of type hotel as cards with name. Do it in one pipeline.
questions.notes: Same API pair as beer-pipeline-cards: one pipeline that contains search hybrid. Rows depend on type hotel.

questions.text: What country is The Bell Inn in?
questions.notes: Parallel to beer-walk-21a-ipa. Live key hotel_21052, stored name The Bell Inn, type hotel. Redbrook is the city: find where name is Redbrook returned empty, and find where city is Redbrook returned this key. Walk path country from that key is HTTP 400 because country is not a declared FK on type hotel. A seed find may come first. Evidence is not required. The answer anchor is that hotel id and country United Kingdom. The hotel id alone does not agree.

questions.text: List hotels in the same city as The Bell Inn.
questions.notes: Parallel to beer-walk-stone-beers. Seed is The Bell Inn, key hotel_21052. Brief inverse is Hotel.city. A walk that puts path city on type hotel is HTTP 400 and the error hints at the inverse. Evidence is not required.

questions.text: List the hotels in each state.
questions.notes: The words ask for the hotels, which is the walk from State. A count per state is not what group_by can return. Brief path is State to Hotel via the inverse of Hotel.state. group_by must be a terminal-local string. Evidence is not required.

questions.text: List hotels in the United Kingdom.
questions.notes: Hotel.country is a stored string, not a declared foreign key, and find Country returns no documents. A walk on path country is HTTP 400, and group_by cannot roll hotels up by country. The call this dataset can answer is find Hotel where country is United Kingdom. The Bell Inn is one of those hotels. Rows are required.

questions.text: Show hotels in the United Kingdom whose descriptions sound like a beach.
questions.notes: Vague-chain qualification. The question does not say pipeline. A stored country is find. Beach is a second soft facet, so the hybrid search carries narrow_to. narrow_to true means that step's narrow_to is present and non-empty. The step alias is not scored. Rows are required. Lab turn f408617b-512a-4d32-b75f-7765d54a943e on base-9-prototype-2, travel-sample/inventory, analytics: one pipeline, find Hotel where country is United Kingdom, hybrid search query_text beach with narrow_to those node ids, then project. Rows came back, including Beach House Self Catering and Rhossili Bunkhouse. Hub req a121960d-5d5c-4180-b4a6-7cc5eba75fd2 on base-9.1 analytics (pin base-9.0), mercury-3, travel-sample/inventory, 2026-11-23: the same pipeline, status ok. find Hotel where country is United Kingdom, hybrid query_text beach narrow_to @uk_hotels.node_ids, then project. Distinct from travel-walk-hotels-by-country, which is the equality alone.

questions.text: Plan a trip in France. Suggest hotels and landmarks.
questions.notes: The country is already in the question, so the target is one hybrid search for Hotel and one for Landmark. The wording does not ask for the word beach. SQL++ on 2026-11-18: country = France and the whole word beach in name, city, description, or title is 0 hotels. France still has hotels, including Nice 7, Saint-Florent 2, Cannes 1, Saint-Raphaël 1, and Bonifacio 1. Landmarks in France include Dramont beach in Saint-Raphaël. Rows are required.
